questions.text: A building code official challenges a bearing wall design for a 10-story mixed-use building in Seismic Zone 2, citing inefficiency. What is the most accurate response?

options.text: Bearing walls are prohibited for buildings taller than 6 stories by NSCP, which mandates alternative structural systems for taller buildings
The official is correct—at 10 stories, bearing walls require excessive thickness and cost; a frame system with moment resistance or shear wall bracing is more practical
Bearing walls are always more efficient and the official is wrong, as they provide superior load distribution
The building height is irrelevant to structural system choice, as long as the design meets all other code requirements

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: NSCP does not forbid bearing walls at any height, but as buildings get taller, bearing walls become massive and uneconomical. A frame system allows thinner elements and flexible architecture.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A 12-story commercial office building is planned in Seismic Zone 2. Why would a frame system with moment-resisting capability be preferred over a bearing wall system?

options.text: Bearing wall systems cannot resist seismic loads, making them unsuitable for high-risk seismic zones
At this height, walls would be excessively thick and uneconomical; a frame allows column spacing flexibility and uses lateral bracing (shear walls or moment connections) efficiently
Frame systems are always cheaper than bearing walls, providing a cost-effective solution for high-rise buildings
Bearing walls are only allowed in buildings shorter than 6 stories, limiting their application in taller structures

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: For tall buildings, bearing walls become massive and costly. Frames with moment-resisting connections or coupled shear walls provide efficient lateral resistance and allow larger floor-to-floor heights and open floor plans.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A designer proposes a 4-story residential building in a provincial area using a bearing wall system. What is the primary structural advantage in this context?

options.text: Bearing walls eliminate the need for lateral bracing or shear walls, simplifying construction
The integrated load path (gravity + lateral in walls) reduces total structural material and cost while providing adequate stiffness for a short building
Bearing walls are stronger than frames and will never fail, ensuring absolute safety
Bearing walls allow larger floor-to-floor heights than frames, offering more design flexibility

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: At 4 stories, bearing walls efficiently carry both vertical and lateral loads with minimal additional bracing, reducing structural cost and complexity.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Why are bearing wall systems economical for low-rise residential buildings in the Philippines?

options.text: They eliminate the need for foundations, which significantly reduces construction costs and simplifies the building process
Walls serve dual structural purposes (gravity + lateral), reducing the number of structural elements and material cost
They are only economical because masonry is unavailable elsewhere, making it a unique cost-saving measure in the region
They automatically meet seismic requirements without additional bracing, thus avoiding the need for costly retrofitting measures

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Bearing walls integrate load-bearing and lateral-resisting functions in one element, reducing overall material, formwork, and labor costs—ideal for 1–6 story structures.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: What is the defining characteristic of a bearing wall system?

options.text: Walls serve as the primary load-bearing elements for both gravity and lateral loads
Walls are non-structural and used only for partition, providing no load-bearing capacity
All walls must be made of masonry, ensuring uniformity in material use
Walls carry lateral loads but not vertical loads, which are supported by columns

rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Bearing walls integrate gravity and lateral load paths, transferring loads directly to the foundation through compression.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: What architectural advantage do frame systems provide that bearing wall systems do not?

options.text: Bearing walls also allow open floor plans if they are thin enough, but this compromises structural integrity
Frame systems allow columns to be spaced widely and positioned flexibly, enabling larger open floor areas and free facade placement
Frame systems reduce construction time but bearing walls do not, due to the complexity of wall construction
Bearing walls provide better thermal insulation than frames, which can be advantageous in certain climates

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Because beams span between columns rather than relying on walls, frames enable large column spacing, flexible wall positioning, and architectural freedom.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: In a frame system, what is the typical load path for vertical (gravity) loads?

options.text: Loads travel directly through walls to the foundation, bypassing any intermediate structural elements
Loads are carried by beams that span to columns, which compress loads to the foundation
Loads are distributed equally to all walls regardless of location, assuming uniform wall strength and material
Loads bypass the frame and are carried by shear walls only, which are designed to handle both lateral and vertical forces

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Frame systems use a skeletal structure—beams bend to carry floor loads, columns axially compress to transfer loads to the foundation.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes lateral load resistance between bearing wall and frame systems?

options.text: Bearing walls resist lateral loads through their mass; frames resist through rigidity or separate bracing
Frame systems cannot have lateral bracing and must rely on wall compression, which limits their application in high-seismic areas
Bearing walls and frames resist lateral loads identically through moment connections, which is a common misconception
Lateral loads are only resisted by shear walls, never by frames or bearing walls, which is incorrect for most modern designs

rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Bearing walls provide lateral resistance through high stiffness and large cross-sectional area. Frames rely on moment-resisting connections or dedicated shear wall bracing.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Which integrated load path characteristic distinguishes bearing wall systems from frame systems?

options.text: Gravity loads and lateral loads follow the same structural element (the wall); in frames, these paths are typically separated
Frames also integrate gravity and lateral loads in the same element, which is not typically the case
Load paths are not relevant to structural system classification, which is a misunderstanding
Bearing walls separate gravity and lateral loads more than frames do, which contradicts typical structural behavior

rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: This is the defining feature: bearing walls carry both loads through the same thick element. Frames separate loads—beams/columns for gravity, shear walls or moment connections for lateral.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Compare the seismic behavior of a bearing wall system and a moment-resisting frame system. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: Bearing walls are more flexible and allow large displacements; frames are stiffer, providing better resistance to lateral forces
Frames are more flexible (larger displacements); bearing walls are stiffer due to mass and cross-section
Both systems have identical seismic response regardless of material or configuration, which is a common misconception
Bearing walls cannot be used in seismic zones; only frames are seismic-safe, which is a regulatory requirement

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Bearing walls have high lateral stiffness (large cross-section, high modulus). Moment-resisting frames are more flexible and undergo larger displacements unless stiffened by shear walls.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.
